Name: twilight_verdict
Title: Twilight Verdict: The Spectral Switch
Experiment: In Twilight Verdict, players engage in a standard social deduction game during the first phase, with each player receiving a hidden role complete with unique abilities and team alignments. The game includes public discussion, private messaging with the GM, and voting rounds. Instead of a timed switch, a dynamic event called the 'Spectral Switch' is triggered when in-game conditions are met—for instance, when suspicion peaks or a critical vote occurs. At this moment, roles, abilities, or allegiances are either revealed or inverted, forcing players to rapidly adapt to a dramatically altered set of rules. Victory conditions are based on cumulative performances across both phases, and new objectives emerge post-switch that may conflict with earlier goals. This twist heightens tension, rewards adaptability, and creates a fresh, unpredictable challenge in social deduction gameplay.

Name: mirror_gambit
Title: Mirror Gambit: The Dual Deception
Experiment: In Mirror Gambit, players begin the game with hidden roles and standard social deduction mechanics such as discussion, voting, and special night actions. Each role possesses a dual aspect: a primary identity and a hidden shadow identity that remains unknown until triggered. The game is divided into two main phases. In the first phase, players work towards traditional victory conditions, aligning subtly with factions (e.g., Protectors vs. Saboteurs) and using their special abilities to gather information. As suspicions peak, a hidden condition known as the 'Mirror Trigger' is met—this might occur after a critical vote or when a specific number of secret messages have been exchanged. Upon triggering, players' shadow identities are activated, causing roles and objectives to be reinterpreted. For example, a Protector might discover a sabotaging shadow, leading to conflicting objectives within the same player. New win conditions emerge in the second phase that depend on the cumulative performance in both parts, as well as on the successful navigation of dual agendas. Key roles include the 'Mirror', who can manipulate the activation timing; the 'Facade', whose apparent loyalty is a ruse; and the 'Double Agent', who benefits from chaos. The implementation involves mechanics for role-based hidden information, dynamic phase transitions, secret communications from the game master that reveal shadow identities, and updated public rules post-trigger. This design emphasizes adaptability, layered strategy, and continuous social interaction, ensuring an engaging experience with high strategic and narrative depth.
